LESSON: READING 1.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORIES (CLASS READER)

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories (Class Reader)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories (Class Reader), part of Strand 1 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you predict the outcome of a story even before you read it? 2. How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. outline the sequence of events in a short story that they have read,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. answer direct and inferential questions from a short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the role of reading in communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. outline the sequence of events in a short story that they have read,

   Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words,

   Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. answer direct and inferential questions from a short story,

   Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. acknowledge the role of reading in communication.

   Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. predict events by focusing on the title and illustrations in a text,

2. silently read the short story,

3. infer contextual meanings of words based on the events in the story,

4. retell the story while citing issues on human rights,

5. role-play selected events and characters in the story,

6. work with peers to discuss the relationships between their own lives and those of characters in the text. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. predict events by focusing on the title and illustrations in a text,
2. silently read the short story,
3. infer contextual meanings of words based on the events in the story,
4. retell the story while citing issues on human rights,
5. role-play selected events and characters in the story,
6. work with peers to discuss the relationships between their own lives and those of characters in the text. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories (Class Reader) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking: It is promoted as the learner assesses the relationship between their own lives and those of the characters in

the story.

• Citizenship: It is promoted as the learner cites issues on human rights.

Values:
Responsibility: It is promoted as the learner takes different roles to dramatise the events in the story.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental and social issues: It is promoted as the learner compares their experiences with those of the characters in the story.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Intensive reading is handled in Kiswahili.

3. answer direct and inferential questions from a short story,
4. acknowledge the role of reading in communication.
